page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals significant performance tradeoffs for this instance. While the 32.0 GB memory capacity is substantial, memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with large-block read-only bandwidth falling into the bottom 10% of tested servers at 22.44 GB/sec. Computational performance is also constrained; both single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores are weak, though single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression achieve average tier performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.ce4.xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration on legacy Intel Xeon hardware, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive CPU throughput. The instance is suited for moderate database operations, caching layers, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint than standard compute instances, provided they are not bottlenecked by the 2 Gbps network baseline or the lower-tier memory transfer speeds.
